properties.name: Yellowstone
properties.description: America's first national park, known for its wildlife and geothermal features, especially Old Faithful geyser.

properties.name: Sequoia
properties.description: Home to giant sequoia trees, including the General Sherman Tree, the largest tree on Earth by volume.

properties.name: Yosemite
properties.description: Famous for its waterfalls, giant sequoias, and spectacular granite cliffs like El Capitan and Half Dome.

properties.name: Mount Rainier
properties.description: An active volcano covered by 26 glaciers, surrounded by subalpine wildflower meadows.

properties.name: Crater Lake
properties.description: The deepest lake in the United States, known for its stunning blue water and clarity.

properties.name: Wind Cave
properties.description: Known for its distinctive boxwork cave formations and one of the world's longest and most complex cave systems.

properties.name: Mesa Verde
properties.description: Preserves the cliff dwellings of the Ancestral Pueblo people, with over 4,700 archaeological sites.

properties.name: Glacier
properties.description: Features pristine forests, alpine meadows, rugged mountains, and spectacular lakes. Home to over 130 named lakes and 1,000 different species of plants.

properties.name: Rocky Mountain
properties.description: Featuring majestic mountain views, alpine tundra ecosystems, and abundant wildlife across more than 415 square miles.

properties.name: Haleakalā
properties.description: Known for its massive dormant shield volcano crater and home to many endangered species found nowhere else on Earth.

properties.name: Hawaii Volcanoes
properties.description: Showcases two of the world's most active volcanoes: Kīlauea and Mauna Loa, allowing visitors to witness geology in action.

properties.name: Lassen Volcanic
properties.description: Features all four types of volcanoes (shield, composite, cinder cone, and plug dome) with hydrothermal areas that include hot springs and mud pots.

properties.name: Denali
properties.description: Home to North America's highest peak, Denali (20,310 feet), and six million acres of pristine wilderness with diverse wildlife.

properties.name: Grand Canyon
properties.description: A massive canyon carved by the Colorado River, up to 18 miles wide and a mile deep, showcasing billions of years of geological history.

properties.name: Zion
properties.description: Known for its massive sandstone cliffs of cream, pink, and red, and its narrow slot canyons and wilderness areas.

properties.name: Acadia
properties.description: The first national park east of the Mississippi River, offering rocky headlands, woodland, and Atlantic shoreline.

properties.name: Hot Springs
properties.description: Preserves 47 natural thermal springs with an average temperature of 143°F. The smallest national park by area, known for its historic bathhouses.

properties.name: Bryce Canyon
properties.description: Famous for its unique geological structures called hoodoos, formed by frost weathering and stream erosion of sedimentary rocks.

properties.name: Grand Teton
properties.description: Features the majestic Teton Range, pristine lakes, and extraordinary wildlife including grizzly bears, moose, and bison.

properties.name: Carlsbad Caverns
properties.description: Features more than 119 limestone caves with spectacular stalactites, stalagmites, and a famous colony of hundreds of thousands of bats.

properties.name: Great Smoky Mountains
properties.description: America's most visited national park, renowned for its diversity of plant and animal life, ancient mountains, and remnants of Southern Appalachian culture.

properties.name: Shenandoah
properties.description: Known for the famous Skyline Drive with stunning vistas, waterfalls, and quiet wooded hollows along the Blue Ridge Mountains.

properties.name: Olympic
properties.description: Encompasses three distinct ecosystems: glacier-capped mountains, old-growth temperate rainforests, and over 70 miles of wild Pacific coastline.

properties.name: Kings Canyon
properties.description: Features one of the deepest canyons in North America and is home to giant sequoia groves and high mountain wilderness.

properties.name: Big Bend
properties.description: Known for its vast expanse of Chihuahuan Desert, ancient limestone canyons carved by the Rio Grande, and isolated mountain ranges.

properties.name: Everglades
properties.description: The largest subtropical wilderness in the United States, protecting rare and endangered species in a vast ecosystem of wetlands and forests.

properties.name: Arches
properties.description: Contains over 2,000 natural stone arches, including the famous Delicate Arch, plus pinnacles, balanced rocks, and other unique geological features.

properties.name: Canyonlands
properties.description: A wilderness of canyons and buttes carved by the Colorado River and its tributaries, divided into four distinct districts.

properties.name: Joshua Tree
properties.description: Named for its distinctive Joshua trees, it straddles the Colorado and Mojave deserts with surreal geological features and stark desert landscapes.

properties.name: Death Valley
properties.description: The hottest, driest, and lowest national park, known for its extreme desert landscapes, salt flats, sand dunes, and mountains.

properties.name: Badlands
properties.description: Features dramatically eroded buttes, pinnacles, and spires amidst the largest undisturbed mixed grass prairie in the United States.

properties.name: Glacier Bay
properties.description: A dynamic glacial landscape with icebergs, temperate rainforest, and deep fjords, home to humpback whales, sea lions, and bald eagles.

properties.name: Voyageurs
properties.description: A water-based park with interconnected waterways, islands, and forests that were once traveled by French-Canadian fur traders (voyageurs).

properties.name: Great Basin
properties.description: Features ancient bristlecone pine forests, limestone caves, and some of the darkest night skies in the contiguous United States.

properties.name: Petrified Forest
properties.description: Known for its large deposits of petrified wood, colorful badlands of the Painted Desert, archaeological sites, and historic structures.

properties.name: Channel Islands
properties.description: Comprises five islands and their ocean environment, preserving unique ecosystems with plants and animals found nowhere else on Earth.

properties.name: Kenai Fjords
properties.description: Protects the Harding Icefield and its outflowing glaciers, and a fjord-rich coastline teeming with marine wildlife.

properties.name: Redwood
properties.description: Protects the world's tallest trees—coast redwoods that can reach over 370 feet—along with vast prairies, oak woodlands, and 40 miles of rugged coastline.

properties.name: Gateway Arch
properties.description: The newest national park, featuring the iconic 630-foot Gateway Arch that commemorates the westward expansion of the United States.

properties.name: Indiana Dunes
properties.description: Features 15 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline with massive sand dunes, wetlands, prairies, and forests containing rare plant species.

properties.name: White Sands
properties.description: Protects the world's largest gypsum dunefield, a stunning landscape of brilliant white sand dunes stretching across 275 square miles.

properties.name: New River Gorge
properties.description: America's newest national park, preserving the New River Gorge and its surrounding Appalachian landscapes, known for whitewater rafting and rock climbing.

properties.name: Biscayne
properties.description: Protects a rare combination of aquamarine waters, emerald islands, and coral reefs just miles from downtown Miami, with 95% of the park being underwater.

properties.name: Dry Tortugas
properties.description: Located 70 miles west of Key West, featuring crystal clear waters, magnificent coral reefs, and the massive 19th century Fort Jefferson.
